en.headline: Disgusting Food Museum continues at Airside until 26 November
en.dek: The Swedish pop-up at Gate33 Gallery in Kai Tak displays more than 80 polarising foods from around the world, with a tasting bar and a vomit bag included with every ticket.
body: The Disgusting Food Museum, a Swedish exhibition that has drawn more than 500,000 visitors internationally, remains open at Gate33 Gallery inside Airside in Kai Tak until 26 November.

The show presents more than 80 foods from about 35 countries across five themed zones, including Swedish fermented herring, Icelandic fermented shark and Sardinian maggot cheese. Organisers said the display explores cultural differences in what people consider edible, alongside notes on insects and cultivated meat as possible future protein sources.

Tickets include a vomit bag. Adult prices are listed at HK$68 on weekdays and HK$88 at weekends and public holidays, with concessions for students, children and seniors. The gallery is open roughly from midday to evening on weekdays and from mid-morning to later evening at weekends.
The exhibition is at Shop 312 on the third floor of Airside. Organisers said the final week offers the last chance to visit before the temporary run ends.

zh.headline: 嘔心食物博物館於啟德AIRSIDE延續至11月26日
zh.dek: 瑞典流行展覽在啟德AIRSIDE的GATE33藝文館展出逾80款爭議美食，門票附送嘔吐袋，並設試食吧。
body: 瑞典「嘔心食物博物館」展覽目前仍在啟德AIRSIDE的GATE33藝文館舉行，至11月26日結束。展覽國際巡迴期間已吸引逾50萬人次參觀。
展覽搜羅來自約35個國家、超過80款具爭議性的食物，分為五大主題展區，包括瑞典鹽醃鮭魚、冰島發酵鯊魚肉及意大利薩丁尼亞活蛆芝士。主辦方指，展覽旨在呈現各地飲食文化差異，並介紹昆蟲及培植肉等未來可能的蛋白質來源。
每張門票附送嘔吐袋。平日成人門票約68元，周末及公眾假期約88元，學生、小童及長者有特惠票。平日開放時間約中午至傍晚，周末則由上午至較晚。
展覽位於AIRSIDE三樓312號舖。主辦方表示，這是最後一週的參觀機會。
